verdicts.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
verdicts.evidence: The Terraform get-started track has a sibling "Convert Terraform HCL to Pulumi" page at /docs/iac/get-started/terraform/convert-hcl/, and pulumi/docs PR #21790 mentions a reference-terraform-state project in the same track. The Terraform integrations hub lists the same five capabilities: "Reference Terraform state: read outputs from Terraform state files so Pulumi and Terraform can manage infrastructure side by side", plus any provider, modules, converting HCL, and orchestration.
verdicts.framing_note: The live next-steps page is the page under review, so it isn't used as evidence. The summary is consistent with the sibling track pages and the integrations hub, but I only confirmed the convert-hcl and reference-state sibling pages directly; I didn't see a page for each of the providers, modules, and orchestration topics.

verdicts.text: HCL code can be converted to Pulumi.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated `pulumi convert` CLI reference lists "Valid source languages: yaml, terraform, bicep, arm, kubernetes" and target languages including typescript and python. That means Terraform HCL code can be converted into Pulumi programs.

verdicts.text: Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together.
verdicts.evidence: This line is a recap bullet ("Orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together"). The only support I found is on other Pulumi docs pages, which don't count as independent proof. The guide's _index.md promises "Orchestration: Managing both tools in unified workflows", and from-terraform.md describes coexisting with Terraform through .tfstate references. I couldn't reach product source because GitHub search hit its rate limit and the guide directory isn't on the default branch.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The claim is vague but plausible: Automation API, the Command provider and terraform state references all make combined workflows possible. Check that the guide really has an orchestration section that backs up this recap bullet.

verdicts.text: `new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` allows reading outputs from another Pulumi stack.
verdicts.evidence: The Node.js SDK defines `StackReference` as a class that "Manages a reference to a Pulumi stack. The referenced stack's outputs are available via..." It has a constructor `(name, args?, opts?)` that falls back to `name` as the referenced stack name when no args are given, and a `getOutput(name)` method that "Fetches the value of the named stack output".
verdicts.framing_note: A bare name like "core-infra" only resolves within the current org/project. To reference a stack in another project, you need the fully qualified name, "org/project/stack".

verdicts.text: Pulumi provides a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource (in `@pulumi/terraform`) that takes `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3.
verdicts.evidence: The `@pulumi/terraform` SDK's `state` module doesn't export an `S3Reference` class or resource. It only exports invoke functions: `export const getS3Reference ... getS3ReferenceOutput`, and likewise for local, remote and AzureRM. So `new terraform.state.S3Reference(name, {bucket, key})` and its `.getOutput(...)` calls won't compile. The `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` form at L203 doesn't exist either.
verdicts.framing_note: The real API is the function `terraform.state.getS3Reference({bucket, key, ...})` or `getS3ReferenceOutput`, which returns outputs. It is not a resource class.

verdicts.text: ### Complex state referencing
verdicts.evidence: The line is just a markdown section heading ("### Complex state referencing"). It doesn't state anything that could be checked as true or false, and it doesn't credit any third-party source. The regex picked up "Complex" as a source name by mistake.
verdicts.framing_note: A heading word was flagged as a source, but no source is actually cited here.

verdicts.text: The `terraform.state.S3Reference` object exposes a `getOutput(name)` method to read Terraform state outputs.
verdicts.evidence: The current @pulumi/terraform Node SDK (sdk/nodejs/state/index.ts) exports only invoke functions: `getS3Reference`/`getS3ReferenceOutput`, `getRemoteReference`, `getLocalReference`, `getAzureRMReference`. It has no `S3Reference` class and no `getOutput(name)` method. You read S3 state outputs from the `outputs` field of the invoke result, not with `new terraform.state.S3Reference(...).getOutput(...)`.
verdicts.source: gh api repos/pulumi/pulumi-terraform/contents/sdk/nodejs/state/index.ts (and the directory listing of sdk/nodejs/state)
verdicts.intuition_flag: This looks like a mix-up with the legacy `RemoteStateReference`/`StackReference.getOutput` API. There is no S3Reference class in any current SDK.

verdicts.text: The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties (logging value "DEFAULT").
verdicts.evidence: I couldn't read the source this session: GitHub search hit its rate limit and the raw-content API call returned an error page. The claim does match the known pulumi-aws/terraform-provider-aws schema. `aws.ecs.Cluster` takes `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` with `kmsKeyId`, `logging` (one of NONE, DEFAULT or OVERRIDE) and `logConfiguration`, so "DEFAULT" is a valid value.
verdicts.source: gh api repos/pulumi/pulumi-aws/contents/sdk/nodejs/ecs/cluster.ts (attempted; rate-limited/error), plus known ClusterConfigurationExecuteCommandConfiguration schema

verdicts.text: `pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says `pulumi import` imports "Resources that are not managed by Pulumi", and it has a `--from string` flag ("Invoke a converter to import the resources"). The Terraform migration guide backs this up: "you can use `pulumi import --from terraform` ... Pulumi will import the resources defined in that file into the stack".

verdicts.text: Pulumi supports transferring state ownership gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
verdicts.evidence: Pulumi's Terraform migration guide describes adopting resources with `pulumi import` (it works on single resources, and `--from terraform` handles a whole .tfstate) and says you can "Coexist with resources provisioned by Terraform or CDKTF by referencing a .tfstate file." Taken together, that supports moving resources over gradually. The per-resource handoff is a manual workflow (import each resource, then run `terraform state rm`), not a dedicated transfer feature.
verdicts.source: https://www.pulumi.com/docs/iac/guides/migration/migrating-to-pulumi/from-terraform/ ; WebSearch ran query "Pulumi migrate from Terraform incrementally resource by resource state"
verdicts.intuition_flag: "Supports transferring state ownership" makes this sound like a built-in feature. In practice it is manual: `pulumi import` per resource plus `terraform state rm`. A third-party guide (encore.dev) also advises splitting ownership at module boundaries rather than per resource.

verdicts.text: The `pulumi import` command takes the form `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says: "If using the command line args directly, the type token, name, id and optional flags must be provided. For example: pulumi import 'aws:iam/user:User' name id". aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc is a valid AWS type token.

verdicts.text: Pulumi provides an 'import API' that can be used programmatically to import resources.
verdicts.evidence: You can import resources programmatically through the Automation API. pulumi/pulumi PR #16721, "Implement Stack.ImportResources() for batch importing resources into a stack via the automation API", was merged 2024-07-19, and #16071 added `--import-file` support to the Automation API. The text under review is only a placeholder code comment ("// Use Pulumi import API to import resources") and doesn't name a real API.
verdicts.source: gh pr list -R pulumi/pulumi --search "automation api import in:title" --state merged
verdicts.intuition_flag: "Import API" isn't a product name. What exists is the Automation API's Stack import method (e.g. Stack.ImportResources in Go), so the comment could name it more precisely.

verdicts.text: Pulumi policies (Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
verdicts.evidence: The Pulumi Policies overview supports the claim: "apply them consistently across resources managed by Pulumi IaC, provisioned with Terraform or CloudFormation, or created manually". Coverage of Terraform resources comes from audit mode, which uses Insights Discovery ("including resources created with Terraform"). Preventative mode only checks Pulumi stack resources during preview/up.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The claim is broadly true, but the PR's example code (validateResourceOfType on aws.ec2.Instance, run as a CrossGuard pack) will only block Pulumi deployments. It won't check Terraform-managed resources unless audit mode is set up through Insights Discovery.

verdicts.text: The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`; policies use `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` and a `validateResource` callback with signature `(resource, args, reportViolation)`.
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi-policy SDK source confirms `export class PolicyPack`, the `EnforcementLevel` type `"advisory" | "mandatory" | "remediate" | "disabled"`, and the SDK's own doc example `validateResource: validateResourceOfType(aws.s3.Bucket, (bucket, args, reportViolation) => {`, which is the same pattern as the doc's code. One nuance: the raw `validateResource` type is `(args: ResourceValidationArgs, reportViolation: ReportViolation)`. The 3-argument `(resource, args, reportViolation)` signature belongs to the callback passed to `validateResourceOfType`, and that is how the doc uses it.
verdicts.framing_note: The claim's wording treats the 3-argument signature as belonging to `validateResource` itself, but it is really the `validateResourceOfType` callback. The doc's code uses it correctly.

verdicts.text: The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can be "public-read" or "public-read-write".
verdicts.evidence: pulumi-aws `sdk/nodejs/s3/bucket.ts` defines `acl` on `aws.s3.Bucket`: "Valid values are `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `aws-exec-read`, `authenticated-read`, and `log-delivery-write`." Note that it is also marked "@deprecated acl is deprecated. Use the aws.s3.BucketAcl resource instead."
verdicts.framing_note: The claim names 2 of the 6 valid canned ACL values. The property is deprecated in favor of aws.s3.BucketAcl, which the doc might want to mention.

verdicts.text: The Pulumi Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi/automation-api-examples repo shows Automation API being embedded in applications, e.g. it can "run Automation API in an HTTP server to expose infrastructure as RESTful resources" using inline programs "constructed and altered on the fly based on input parsed from user-specified POST bodies". It ships for Go, Node.js, Python, C#, and Java.

verdicts.text: The Automation API is imported from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` and provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` with `stackName`, `projectName`, `program` options, plus `stack.setConfig` and `stack.up({ onOutput })` returning `outputs`.
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi/pulumi sdk/nodejs/automation/localWorkspace.ts source (shipped as `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`) defines `static async createOrSelectStack(args: InlineProgramArgs, opts?: LocalWorkspaceOptions): Promise<Stack>`, and inline args are routed through `inlineSourceStackHelper`. I didn't read the InlineProgramArgs fields (stackName/projectName/program) or Stack's `setConfig`/`up({ onOutput })` returning UpResult.outputs in this session. Those parts are standard Automation API surface, but they were not directly quoted.

verdicts.text: The `terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` from the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import.
verdicts.evidence: The `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` module has no `terraform` namespace. Its index.ts only re-exports "./cmd", "./config", "./errors", "./stack", "./stackSettings", "./projectSettings", "./localWorkspace", "./workspace", "./events", "./remoteStack", "./remoteWorkspace" and "./tag", so `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` at L203 won't resolve. Terraform state references come from the separate `@pulumi/terraform` package, which is how the same page imports them at L245.
verdicts.intuition_flag: I didn't check whether `S3Reference` exists in `@pulumi/terraform` at all. I believe that package offers `RemoteStateReference` / `state.getLocalReference`-style APIs instead, so that is worth confirming.

verdicts.text: The `aws.ecs.Service` resource accepts `cluster`, `taskDefinition`, and `desiredCount` arguments.
verdicts.evidence: The generated pulumi-aws Node.js SDK declares `cluster` ("ARN of an ECS cluster") and `desiredCount` ("Number of instances of the task definition to place and keep running") on `aws.ecs.Service`. Its own examples pass all three arguments, e.g. `cluster: exampleAwsEcsCluster.id, taskDefinition: exampleAwsEcsTaskDefinition.arn, desiredCount: 1`.

verdicts.text: Component resources can wrap Terraform-managed infrastructure so that platform teams handle multi-tool complexity while developers create resources without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources.
verdicts.evidence: The components concept page says components let "consumers create complex infrastructure through a simple, well-defined interface—without needing to know the implementation details." The pulumi-terraform package lets a component read Terraform state outputs internally, so the claim that a component can wrap Terraform-managed infrastructure out of the consumer's sight follows from that.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The example code on L248 uses `terraform.state.S3Reference`. I couldn't confirm that type exists (gh hit a rate limit), and the known API is `terraform.state.RemoteStateReference`, so that code is worth checking separately.

verdicts.text: `pulumi.ComponentResource` is the base class for components, with a constructor calling `super(type, name, {}, opts)` and `registerOutputs`.
verdicts.evidence: The example (L254-260, L305) extends `pulumi.ComponentResource`, calls `super("custom:WebApplication", name, {}, opts)`, and calls `this.registerOutputs({...})`. That fits the @pulumi/pulumi Node SDK, where ComponentResource is exported from sdk/nodejs/resource.ts with a `(type, name, args, opts)` constructor and a `registerOutputs` method. I read sdk/nodejs/resource.ts, but the output was cut off before the ComponentResource class body. The part I saw only shows the SDK's doc comments referring to ComponentResource, so I couldn't quote the constructor signature itself.
